scope: Two suspect items (P1-ED-010, P1-ED-014) + cross-referenced items from S809.2 Agent B Defect Manifest (P1-EC-020, P1-ED-051)
methodology: Direct line-level inspection of pack_d_corrected.js and pack_c_corrected.js. For each EW slot: compare text content against the choice text at the matched letter position to determine if the explanation semantically describes that choice.
architecture_note: Pack D Section E items (ED-010, ED-014, ED-051) are SINGLE-OBJECT format — ExplanationWrong fields and content-block fields (Stem, Choices, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect) exist within the same JSON object. Contrary to the S809 EW Integrity Audit's claim of 'Dual-object (metadata block with EW fields + content block with EC/Stem/Choices/CC),' no paired-object architecture was observed for these items.

dl010_evidence.stem: Juniperfield grants employees system access limited only to what is necessary to perform their specific job duties. What security principle is being applied?

choices.A: The principle of maximum access for efficiency

EW_D.text: Management override is bypassing controls, not a principle for limiting user access.

EW_D.match_assessment: MATCH — The text correctly identifies what management override is (bypassing controls) and explains why it is wrong for this question (it is not a principle for limiting user access, i.e., not least privilege). The phrase 'limiting user access' directly relates to the question's concept of least privilege.
EW_D.note: Agent B incorrectly claimed the phrase 'limiting user access' is unrelated to the question. Agent B described ED-010 as 'the question about independent verification / preventive controls' — this is wrong. ED-010 is about access control / least privilege, making 'limiting user access' perfectly on-topic.

dl010_evidence.misassignment_detail: The only non-empty EW slot (EWD) correctly explains why choice D (Management override) is wrong for a least-privilege question. No cross-item contamination detected. Agent B's DL-010 flag on this item appears to be based on a misidentification of the question's topic.

dl010_evidence.stem: Northfell has a supervisor recount inventory counted by warehouse staff before finalizing the count. What type of control activity is this?

choices.A: A physical control over inventory storage only
choices.B: Independent verification, checking the accuracy of work performed by others
choices.C: A preventive control that stops errors before they occur
choices.D: Segregation of duties, since only one person performs the recount

EW_D.text: Segregation of duties separates incompatible responsibilities; a one-person recount by a supervisor is independent verification, not the segregation concept itself.

EW_D.attached_to_choice: D — Segregation of duties, since only one person performs the recount
EW_D.match_assessment: MATCH — The text correctly identifies what segregation of duties is (separating incompatible responsibilities) and explains why D is wrong for this independent-verification question (the supervisor's recount is independent verification, not segregation). The explanation is choice-specific and concept-accurate.
EW_D.note: This is a clean, well-written distractor explanation. It teaches the distinction between segregation of duties and independent verification — a core CMA Part 1 concept.

dl010_evidence.misassignment_detail: The only non-empty EW slot (EWD) correctly explains why choice D (Segregation of duties) is wrong for an independent-verification question. No DL-010 misassignment detected.

dl010_evidence.stem: Thornfield stores inventory in a locked warehouse accessible only to authorized personnel with badge access. What type of control is this?

choices.A: An entity-level control unrelated to specific assets
choices.B: A detective control performed after the fact only
choices.C: A compensating control for a segregation of duties gap
choices.D: A physical control that restricts access to assets

EW_A.text: Entity-level controls set the overall tone and governance structure for the organization. Here, the described badge-access warehouse is a specific, targeted physical safeguard over a particular asset class, not a broad entity-level policy.

EW_B.text: The control is not only detective after the fact; restricted access helps prevent unauthorized physical handling or removal.

EW_C.text: A compensating control offsets another weakness, such as limited segregation; the stem describes a direct physical access control.

EW_A.attached_to_choice: A — An entity-level control unrelated to specific assets
EW_A.match_assessment: MATCH — Explains why A is wrong (entity-level = broad governance vs. this is a specific physical safeguard).

EW_B.attached_to_choice: B — A detective control performed after the fact only
EW_B.match_assessment: MATCH — Explains why B is wrong (control is not only detective — restricted access is preventive).

EW_C.attached_to_choice: C — A compensating control for a segregation of duties gap
EW_C.match_assessment: MATCH — Explains why C is wrong (compensating controls offset weaknesses; this is a direct physical access control).

dl010_evidence.misassignment_detail: All three non-empty EW slots correctly describe their attached choices. Agent B claimed that EC-020's distractors were about 'monthly bank reconciliation' and 'quarterly audit review' — those are actual distractors from EC-022 (preventive vs. detective duplicate-payment control), not EC-020. Agent B confused EC-020 with EC-022.

dl010_evidence.stem: Briarcliff requires multi-factor authentication for all employees accessing financial systems remotely. What is the primary purpose of this control?

choices.A: To replace the need for segregation of duties
choices.B: To ensure compliance with balanced scorecard metrics
choices.C: To reduce the risk of unauthorized access to financial systems and data
choices.D: To eliminate the need for any other IT general controls

EW_B.text: This option reflects a misunderstanding of password access authentication control. The choice "To ensure compliance with balanced scorecard metrics" is inconsistent with the correct treatment under CMA Part 1 guidelines for this topic area. Review the applicable costing standard or framework to understand why this approach is not appropriate.
EW_B.status: DL-013 boilerplate — 307 chars. Template text with minimal educational value, but CORRECTLY assigned to slot B.

EW_B.attached_to_choice: B — To ensure compliance with balanced scorecard metrics
EW_B.match_assessment: MATCH — The boilerplate text directly quotes choice B's text ('To ensure compliance with balanced scorecard metrics') and identifies it as inconsistent. While the text is generic boilerplate (DL-013), it is correctly assigned to slot B.
EW_B.note: Agent B claimed this had text-to-slot mismatch: 'template text references balanced scorecard metrics (choice A) but assigned to slot B.' This is incorrect — 'balanced scorecard metrics' IS choice B's text, not choice A. Choice A is 'replace the need for segregation of duties.' No misassignment.

dl010_evidence.misassignment_detail: EWB is DL-013 boilerplate (low educational value) but is correctly assigned — the text describes and quotes choice B. Agent B's claim of text-to-slot mismatch appears to be based on confusing which choice contains which text.

additional_dl010_items_found.finding: NO DL-010. All three EW slots correctly describe their attached choices. Agent B confused EC-020's distractors with EC-022's distractors.
NO DL-010. EWB is DL-013 boilerplate but correctly assigned to slot B. Agent B's text-to-slot mismatch claim was based on confusing choice A and choice B's text.

summary.overall_assessment: ZERO DL-010 confirmed across all 4 investigated items. All non-empty ExplanationWrong fields correctly describe their attached choices.

false_positive_details.P1-EC-020: Agent B confused EC-020 (physical controls) with EC-022 (preventive vs. detective duplicate payment). EC-020's actual EW slots are all correctly assigned.
false_positive_details.P1-ED-010: Agent B confused ED-010 (access control / least privilege) with ED-014 (independent verification). ED-010's EWD correctly describes management override for a least-privilege question. The phrase 'limiting user access' is on-topic.
false_positive_details.P1-ED-051: Agent B claimed text-to-slot mismatch (boilerplate describes choice A but assigned to slot B). In reality, the boilerplate correctly quotes choice B's text ('balanced scorecard metrics'). Choice A is 'segregation of duties' — not what the boilerplate references.

summary.root_cause_of_false_positives: Agent B appears to have cross-referenced items from different rotation groups or confused which choices belong to which QID. For EC-020 vs EC-022, the error was a complete QID mix-up. For ED-010 vs ED-014, the error was topic misidentification. For ED-051, the error was expecting text in slot A that was actually in slot B.
summary.remaining_concerns: While DL-010 is not present, other defect classes apply: DL-026 (53 empty non-CC slots across all 38 seeds), DL-013 (9 boilerplate slots in 5 Pack D seeds), and weak EC quality on several items. See S809 EW Integrity Audit and S809.2 Defect Manifest for full remediation scope.
